[attribute-designator]
=== `@designator` Designator of Journal Edition/Version

This attribute was inherited from JATS and _does not_ have anything to do with a standard’s designation. The attribute is used to hold the edition number, version number, or similar publishing identifier (for a journal, book, etc.) as an unadorned numeric or alphabetic value for machine comparisons.

#### Usage/Remarks
#### Standards Designation

The standards designation is tagged with the <<element-std-ref,`<std-ref>`>> element.
#### Use for Book and Journals

When an edition, version, or similar statement concerning a journal contains ordinals (such as “`3rd`”) or words such as “`3rd print edition`”, this attribute can preserve the edition/version number as a simple, machine-processable number, such as “`3`”.

#### OPTIONAL on many elements; click for list and usage

<<element-edition,`<edition>`>>, <<element-extended-by,`<extended-by>`>>, <<element-restricted-by,`<restricted-by>`>>, <<element-version,`<version>`>>
|===
| Value| Meaning

| Text, numbers, or special characters| Machine processable version of an edition/version number for journal articles.
| Restriction| This is an optional attribute; there is no default.
|===
